title: The number pyramid
segments: Xian fills this grid with numbers. He places the numbers from one to five in the five squares in the bottom row, in some order. In the next two rows, each square contains the sum of the numbers in the three closest squares in the row below. The arrows indicate how this addition works for the first square in the second row. What is the largest possible value of the number in the top square?
This is a maximising problem. We will count how often each bottom number contributes.
The centre counts three times, its neighbours twice, and the ends once.
Put five centrally, three and four beside it, and one and two at the ends.
Larger numbers in more-counted positions give a larger total.
The middle sums are nine, twelve, eleven. The maximum is thirty-two: answer C.
